Extremely disappointing experience. I went in with an inspiration photo and asked for a soft, warm, blended balayage. I completely understood that it wouldn’t be an exact copy, but what I received was nowhere near the overall look I had asked for - the colour was very cool and ashy, with very obvious lighter pieces and money pieces that made it look much more like highlights.

I left the salon and was told by the stylist to contact her on Instagram if I had any issues. I did exactly that as soon as I got home and saw the colour properly in natural light. Instead of actually listening to my concerns, I was repeatedly told that the salon was “happy with the result”. That is completely irrelevant when the customer who paid for it is not happy with the result.

I was offered the opportunity to return, but after the way my complaint was handled I did not trust the salon to correct my hair. I have since had another professional stylist assess it and I’m now paying a further £85 to have the colour corrected.

The customer service has honestly been just as disappointing as the hair. Samantha, the owner, was extremely dismissive and told me they would no longer communicate with me by email. Shortly afterwards, the salon posted Instagram stories about customers “scamming” businesses, followed by posts about inspiration photos, “unrealistic expectations” and how they are “not magicians”. Given the timing, this came across as incredibly unprofessional and petty.

I never expected an exact replica of the inspiration photo. I expected the salon to listen to what I actually wanted and to take my concerns seriously when the result wasn’t what I asked for.

I have never experienced customer service like this from a salon. I’m extremely disappointed and would absolutely not recommend Salon Seven.

I am a bet365 customer and voluntarily supplied detailed evidence concerning “Mr Jay Bets / Fixed Football Games”, including “100% fixed” claims, betting screenshots, timestamps, specific fixtures, crypto-payment evidence and a Report Fraud reference.

I never alleged bet365 was involved in the alleged scam or asked bet365 to refund my crypto payment. I simply asked for the evidence to be preserved and properly assessed by Trading Risk / Sports Integrity / Compliance.

Instead, Customer Complaints Supervisor Liam S initially told me there was “no integrity concern” and effectively “nothing bet365 could do”, without confirming whether the specialist integrity teams had actually reviewed the fixtures, markets, screenshots or internal/IBIA data.

After I challenged this, bet365 still would not confirm whether that specialist review had taken place. Their latest response then restricted discussion to my own account/transactions and warned that further correspondence may not receive a reply.

I have never asked for confidential customer information or details of a live investigation. I asked one simple question: was the evidence properly routed, preserved and professionally assessed before Customer Complaints reached its conclusion?

Given bet365’s size, regulatory responsibilities, safer-gambling commitments and IBIA participation, the handling has been dismissive and unacceptable. The evidence and bet365’s own responses have now been supplied to the UK Gambling Commission SBIU and IBIA.

Never have I experienced something so disorganised and unprofessional. I absolutely would not recommend this car park!

We arrived around 4am, approximately 2.5 hours before our flight. The car park was pitch black, and the road leading up to it was absolutely atrocious. We were told the minibus was on its way back and would be with us within 20 minutes. However, we ended up waiting over an hour.

When the minibus finally arrived, everyone piled on and we loaded our luggage, only to discover there were no seats available. At this point, we had around 1.5 hours until our flight and were understandably starting to panic. We repeatedly asked what was going to happen, and we were eventually told that someone would drive our car to the terminal. At the time, we didn't really have a choice — we just needed to get to the airport.

This took at least another 15 minutes, meaning we arrived at the terminal with just one hour until our flight. We then had to check in our buggy, get through security and make our way to the gate.

Thankfully, the special assistance worker was absolutely fantastic and fast-tracked us through the airport. Without her help, there is no way we would have made our flight.

The whole experience was incredibly stressful and completely avoidable. The organisation was shocking from start to finish, and I would never, ever book with this car park again. Absolutely appalling service.

Re: Airport Parking - Dreadful, and just pleased to have left with our car! Please safe yourself the stress and do not use. As others have said:
- Greeted with an additional charge.
- At Pickup, our flight was an hour late, arriving middle of the night, and we were left outside for over an hour waiting for their transport despite trying to call and text to regularly communicate our progress through arrivals. They would not answer, or just hang up.
- Many others were also waiting, some for over 2 hours.
- When the bus arrived there were not enough seats, some had to get a taxi, others just sent one driver to get the car and return for others.
- Some were charged extra for a late inbound flight.

Avoid.

Very disappointed with my experience with Comms Express.

I placed my order on 20 August 2026 after being promised next-day delivery. Amy, a member of the sales team, initially quoted me £159.77 for the intercom. However, when I received the payment link, the price had increased to £162.43. When I questioned this, I was told that the system had changed the price. I paid £162.43, which included the intercom, adapter and next-day delivery.

Unfortunately, I did not receive the order the next day. The intercom arrived four days later, and I am still waiting for the adapter. I have now been told that the adapter will not arrive until 4 September 2026.

I find this extremely disappointing. I paid for next-day delivery and for the adapter, yet neither the promised delivery time nor the complete order was provided.

The communication and customer service have been very disappointing, and the whole experience has caused me unnecessary inconvenience.

Based on my experience, I would not recommend Comms Express and I hope the company improves its customer service and delivery commitments.

one_star_reviews.text:
I normally wouldn’t post something like this publicly, but I feel people in Chelmsford should know what my experience with the C&E Centre mental health team has been like.

I have been known to multiple mental health services over the years and I have honestly never felt as failed, ignored and dismissed as I have by this particular service.

When I was released from prison, I went straight to the C&E Centre myself because I knew I needed help. I didn’t hide anything. I was completely honest about where my head was at, how much I was struggling and how badly I needed support. I explained that within the previous 13 months I had been sectioned, and that my partner and I had recently had a newborn baby.

Six weeks later, I have heard NOTHING.

My GP has chased them. Probation has chased them. I am still left sitting here feeling trapped, isolated and without the support I actively asked for.

What makes it worse is that during the appointment I was actually told that because I had not engaged properly with services in the past, they might not offer me anything.

How is that acceptable?

Mental health services constantly tell people to reach out, speak up and ask for help. Then when someone finally does exactly that, they are judged on their past and potentially written off because they struggled to engage before.

Surely anyone working in mental health should understand that poor engagement can itself be part of someone being mentally unwell.

I walked through their door voluntarily after prison and admitted I needed help. I swallowed my pride and was honest. Instead of feeling supported, I have been left feeling like I am being punished for my past.

People should not have to reach breaking point before somebody decides they are worth helping.

For a service supposedly there to support vulnerable people, the communication and follow-up I have experienced has been absolutely disgraceful.

If this is what “reaching out for help” looks like, it is no wonder people lose faith in mental health services.

one_star_reviews.text:
I would strongly recommend that landlords carefully consider whether Flatfair is the right deposit scheme for them.

I submitted a claim for £1,440 following a tenancy of approximately 3½ years, supported by the checkout report, invoices and other evidence. I accepted that fair wear and tear had to be taken into account and deliberately limited my claim rather than seeking to recover all of the costs I had incurred.

The claim was ultimately rejected in full. My biggest concern was that an interim inspection report from 2023, which formed part of the evidence submitted, recorded the property as being in good condition during the tenancy. Despite this, the adjudication decision placed considerable weight on the absence of a check-in report from the start of the tenancy and awarded £0.

I appreciate that adjudication has to be evidence-based and that the absence of a proper check-in inventory was a weakness in my case. However, I was disappointed that the 2023 inspection evidence did not appear to receive meaningful consideration when assessing whether deterioration had occurred during the tenancy.

As a landlord, I found the outcome extremely frustrating, particularly having incurred considerably more in remedial costs than I was actually claiming. Following this experience, I would personally prefer to use a traditional deposit scheme in future and would advise other landlords to carefully consider the differences before choosing Flatfair.

Update:
Following my critical review on this website (I had not contacted them) Flatfair referred the case back to its independent adjudication service for a fresh review by a different adjudicator. The revised outcome awarded £150, leaving £1,290 of my claim unsuccessful.

For landlords considering Flatfair, my experience has highlighted some significant risks:

• No FCA-regulated insurance protection: Flatfair confirms that its No Deposit product is not insurance. It operates on a discretionary basis rather than providing the same model as a traditional cash deposit scheme.

• Zero leverage: In my opinion, a non-refundable fee gives tenants considerably less financial incentive to protect a property than having a substantial refundable cash deposit at stake. This is one of the fundamental differences between the two models.

• Risk ultimately sits with the landlord: The convenience of a deposit-free scheme may benefit tenants and agents, but my experience has left me questioning whether it provides sufficient protection for landlords when there is a dispute.

Despite the second arbitration my experience has not changed my view. I am still awaiting to receive my paltry compensation as well. In my opinion, the convenience of a deposit-free scheme is not worth the additional risk, and I would choose a traditional five-week cash deposit scheme for future tenancies.

Based on my experience, I would not use Flatfair again and urge all landlords to avoid.

one_star_reviews.text: I would give them 0 if I could. They happily took my money in October 2024 for an ASD & ADHD assessment, then they refused to send me anything regarding the assessment until I had discharged myself from my therapist. I was quoted 12 weeks from start to finish when I paid. It took them 1 month to send me the initial questionnaires, then as I didn't have any support, I had to drop out of university as I couldn't take it anymore. In January 2025, after liaising between my GP, my university and RTN, they sent me a link to book an assessment for February. I had little to no correspondence during that time. The assessment itself was decent, taking about 3 hours in total (credit to the clinician, not the company itself). At the end of the assessment, I was quoted 3 weeks to get the report. 4 weeks passed and I recieved no communication and no report. Eventually when I did get through, they extended it to 6 weeks, after 6 weeks I heard nothing. After prying information out of these people by emailing and calling daily, they extended it to 8, then 10, then 12 weeks. Eventually, 14 weeks post assessment, I recieved the diagnostic report after taking it up with management/the ICB. So a "12 week" timeframe was actually 10 months - and in that time frame I was forced to drop out of uni, I lost my job and my mental health declined. Once I recieved my report, shared care was denied by my GP so I got back in touch and they quoted around £700 for the medication titration pathway which I just couldn't afford as all of my money went on the assessment. Eventually I switched GP and was re-referred to RTN through Right To Choose. I was placed on a waitlist in July 2025 and given an appointment for October 2025 to begin titration. A week after recieving this appointment email, they got back to me and said they had removed me from the wait list and put me on a different list indefinitely as they had "unresolved issues with the ICB". I'd had enough so I went straight to the ICB and my GP as I was going back to university for my final year and had exercised all of my years of student loan, so this was my final chance to complete it. The ICB promptly responded and stated that they knew nothing of this and that RTN had no reason to say this. My impression was that they were just trying to push me to go private so they could get an extra £700 out of me. After the head of the ICB in my area got in contact with RTN, they quickly changed their tune and put me back on the medication pathway with an appointment for September 2025. I sent a formal complaint which they rejected and quoted the small print, with their loophole being the word "estimated 12 weeks". Titration was going well until my mother was diagnosed with breast cancer and an appointment slipped my mind - I was preoccupied with supporting my family and forgot to communicate that I couldn't do the appointment that day. After getting back into contact with them, it took them approx a month to reply to my 4 emails after I called. They told me they would pass my request to remain on my dose and discharge me on, as it would be my final appointment before being discharged on that dose. Instead of doing this, I recieved an email to say I'd been discharged from the service before my final appointment due to inconsistency and no shows. What concerned me most was that I did not see any clear notice on the menu stating that a 10% service charge would be added. The only additional charge I noticed on the menu was a small note stating a £1 per person tea charge.

When it came to payment, I was not given an itemised bill showing a service charge. I was simply told a total of £129 on a calculator, which was then reduced to £120.

Only after I left, calculated the menu prices myself (£117), and returned to question the amount was I told that a 10% service charge had been added.

When I asked for that charge to be removed, instead of simply explaining the policy, I was asked, “Don’t you pay service charge when you eat out?” and was eventually told that I would not be welcome at the restaurant again.

They eventually refunded £3, leaving the final amount I paid at £117.

My concern is not about £3. It is about transparency and the way a customer was treated for questioning an additional charge that had not been clearly explained to me.

If a restaurant intends to add a service charge, customers should be clearly informed of it before ordering and should be able to understand exactly how their final bill has been calculated. A customer should also be able to question a charge without being mocked or told they are no longer welcome.

I have eaten at many restaurants across the UK, including both casual and Michelin-starred restaurants, and I have never experienced this kind of response simply for asking for clarification about a service charge.

I will not be returning.

one_star_reviews.text:
purchased a Thinkware F790 dashcam from TrackerShop with professional installation, specifically because I wanted reliable parking recording and evidence should my car be hit whilst parked.

Unfortunately, I’ve had repeated issues with the dashcam since installation. The original installation was subsequently found to have been incorrectly wired and remedial work was carried out. Despite this, I continued to experience problems with the dashcam recording whilst parked.

The issue became particularly serious when my car was subsequently hit whilst parked. When I checked the dashcam, I discovered that there was no footage of the incident, leaving me without potentially important evidence for my insurer or the police.

I’ve spent months going back and forth with TrackerShop and Thinkware, carrying out troubleshooting and having multiple engineers attend. Thinkware’s investigations also identified a power-loss issue and referred the matter back to TrackerShop.

I have now had the dashcam removed following a further engineer inspection and am seeking a refund and compensation. However, despite the length of time this complaint has been ongoing, I am still waiting for TrackerShop to provide a resolution.

I appreciate that technical faults can happen, but what has been most disappointing is the amount of time, chasing and effort I’ve had to put into resolving an issue with a product that was professionally supplied and installed. I would have expected much better communication and ownership of the problem.

At the time of writing, my complaint remains unresolved.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely disappointed with the customer service

I ordered a home study book from this company in April. What makes this even more frustrating is that the legislation changed just two days later.

As a transport compliance company, they should have been fully aware that these legislative changes were coming. In my opinion, they had a responsibility to at least inform customers that an updated edition was about to be released, or advise customers to delay their purchase by a couple of days.

Instead, after I contacted them and politely asked if they could simply send me the few updated sections affected by the new legislation, they refused. Their only solution was for me to buy the entire new study book.

I wasn't asking for a free new book — only the handful of pages containing the changes, so I could continue studying the correct legislation.

I find that incredibly poor customer service. A company specialising in transport compliance should put accuracy and customer support before trying to sell the same customer another book just days after their original purchase.

Very disappointed. I genuinely expected much better.

3-Month Update – Very Disappointed
Unfortunately, my experience after only three months is completely different from my original review.
The hair system started losing its colour very quickly and no longer matched my natural hair after only 2 weeks. I had to dye it regularly, but even then the colour would only last a few days before fading again.
The system also started shedding hair much sooner than I expected. After around three months, it had deteriorated to the point where I needed a replacement. For something that was professionally supplied and fitted, I expected it to last considerably longer.
As SF Hair did not have a replacement system available in the correct colour, I had to purchase a new matching hair system online myself. I then contacted the hairdresser who originally fitted mine and asked if they could refit the replacement. I was told they would not fit a system that had not been purchased from them, apparently due to their policy and insurance reasons.
I found this extremely disappointing. After paying for the original service and experiencing problems with the colour, excessive shedding and very short lifespan, I expected some level of aftercare or support. Instead, I was effectively left to deal with the problem myself.
My initial experience was very positive, which makes the lack of support afterwards even more disappointing. Based on my experience over these three months, I feel very let down and that the focus was more on selling another system than supporting an existing customer.

one_star_reviews.text:
Formal Complaint – Misleading Advertising

I booked this property because I had stayed there previously and because it advertised a bar, breakfast and ample parking. These facilities were important to us as my wife, my 83-year-old mother and I were travelling back from France.

Before arriving, at around 9:30 pm, I called the hotel and was told the bar was open until 11:00 pm. We arrived at 10:10 pm, only to be told the bar was closed. I was also told that breakfast was no longer offered, despite it still being advertised when I booked.

My 83-year-old mother has COPD. There was no lift, and we were given a room up three steep flights of stairs. Despite explaining her condition, staff showed little concern and offered no alternative.

There was also no available parking, despite "ample parking" being advertised. I eventually had to park beside an area where work was being carried out.

Because the advertised bar was closed, I had to spend around an hour late at night finding an off-licence and did not get to bed until after 1:00 am. I then had to go out the following morning to find breakfast.

When I requested a refund, the staff member refused and claimed these facilities were not advertised on Booking.com. I showed him the listing on my phone, after which he went into the office. I am extremely concerned that the information may subsequently have been changed.

Most importantly, I am very concerned that the hotel's response to Booking.com did not accurately reflect what happened.

I ask Booking.com to investigate the original listing, the hotel's response and any subsequent changes to the advertised facilities. Given the circumstances and the clear difference between what was advertised and what was provided, I believe a full refund is justified.

one_star_reviews.text:
I am extremely disappointed and angry about how this issue was handled.

When we moved into the property in April 2023, I noticed that the external opening for the kitchen extractor was only 100mm, despite the manufacturer’s installation instructions clearly specifying a 150mm duct/outlet. The manufacturer’s guide also indicates approximately 100% performance with 150mm, 80% with 125mm and only 65% with 100mm.

I raised this with the builder and he agreed to come back and rectify it when he had time.

I trusted him. I waited.

I followed up on 9 May 2023, 29 May 2023, 10 July 2023, 22 March 2025, 21 September 2025 and 26 September 2025. On 1 October 2025, he finally replied and said that he would come when he had time.

He never came.

I then contacted him another eight times. He did not respond to a single one of those messages.

Meanwhile, we continued to live with an extractor that performed extremely poorly. Smoke and cooking smells would spread throughout the house and upstairs. This was not a minor inconvenience — it went on for years.

I even obtained a quotation from another contractor and offered him a straightforward solution: if he was too busy to come himself, I would arrange another contractor to carry out the work, with the cost covered by him.

He ignored that as well.

Eventually, I had to arrange for the problem to be dealt with myself.

And this is when I discovered just how poor the original installation actually was.

If I had not noticed the 100mm opening in the first place, I would never have asked for it to be corrected, and I would never have had any reason to open up the extractor and see what was underneath.

Once the cover was removed, I found several excessive bends and twists in the ducting, rather than a reasonably direct route. The duct was further restricted at the internal connection, and the ducting appeared to have been secured using ordinary adhesive tape rather than proper duct clamps. Part of the ducting had also become loose/disconnected.

Seeing the workmanship behind the cover was extremely disappointing. It gave me the impression that the installation had simply been completed and covered up, without proper attention being given to the quality and standard of the work underneath.

This was not what I expected from a professional installation. The manufacturer’s instructions clearly provide guidance on the required duct size and routing, yet what I found inside was a very different story.

The remedial work has now been completed. The ducting has been rerouted much more directly, properly connected and secured, and the external opening has been corrected.

What makes me most angry is not simply that the original installation was poor. Mistakes can happen. It is the complete lack of responsibility afterwards.

I gave this builder years to put the problem right. He agreed to come. He did not come. I followed up repeatedly. He stopped responding. I even offered a practical alternative so that he would not have to come himself.

At some point, “I’ll come when I have time” has to mean something.

Instead, I was left to live with the consequences of the installation for years and eventually deal with the problem myself.

I find this extremely disappointing and, frankly, very frustrating. A professional should not simply walk away from a problem they have agreed to rectify.

Mistakes can be forgiven. Ignoring the customer, failing to honour your commitment and refusing to take responsibility are much harder to accept.

I went in with two reference photos and attempted to discuss it with the barber who unfortunately had limited English speaking skills (and barber skills I would soon learn).

After about 10 seconds, the barber lost patience with me trying to discuss the styles, made me put my phone away and just asked if I wanted the sides trimmed. I sheepishly agreed because he was acting like he'd got the picture. This red flag should've been enough for me to leave so please learn from my mistake if this ever happens to you.
When he was done ruining my hair, I complimented the clean finish he had done to my ends, and I very politely pointed out that the rest wasn't what I asked for and suggested we can salvage it by going a little shorter on the sides.
He immediately threw his hands up, rolled his eyes and looked at his supervisor as if I had done something wrong. This manchild's reaction was completely disgraceful and unprofessional, and the vibe from there was very tense and uncomfortable.

When all was said and done and I was leaving, the barber was looking at my hair with wide eyes, I think he knew it was a botch job. i it was mortifying for all involved.
I genuinely wondered if it was intentional, I had asked him to leave my fringe resting at my eyebrows, and he cut it a full inch above them in a perfectly straight horrible line. How skill-less do you have to be to make that mistake?

I travelled very far to get my hair cut here before starting a big trip, so I am very disappointed to have walked out with a much worse trim than I went in with. I will never step near this place again.

P.S. For context, I brought in two reference photos showing trimmed-top and curtain-bang hairstyles. I've done this many times and obviously know you can't have both at once. Good barbers discuss the references with you and agree on something that best suits what you're looking for. In fact, some of the best barbers I've had have specifically spoken poorly of barbers who react negatively to anything beyond a simple request instead of actually engaging with the customer.

My criticism is primarily directed at the unprofessionalism and botch job from the specific "barber" I was unfortunate enough to be seated with, but I'm disappointed with the wider establishment too. The supervisor sided with his guy rather than acknowledge his embarrassing behaviour when I politely suggested shortening the sides a little more. I don't think it's too much to expect a barber to engage with you about your hairstyle, or to accept polite feedback when you're not satisfied with their work.

one_star_reviews.text:
Absolutely appalling service from Apex Law. I would give 0 stars if I could.

A straightforward no-chain purchase that should have taken around six weeks dragged on for SEVEN MONTHS, eventually requiring my mortgage offer to be extended and causing an enormous amount of completely unnecessary stress.

The lack of communication was beyond unacceptable. Emails ignored, calls unanswered, voicemail full, vague updates and constantly being told we were “still waiting for enquiries” without clear explanations or updated reports. I felt like I was harassing them for basic information about the largest purchase of my life.

I only spoke to my solicitor, Ismail Gozde, on the phone once in seven months. The final report was delayed without proper communication and, immediately after I complained, it was sent. He then went on two weeks’ annual leave.

The ONLY reason this sale finally went through was because my mortgage advisor personally called my solicitor on his mobile and pushed him to complete the report. If I hadn’t repeatedly chased and complained, I genuinely believe I’d still be waiting.

The seller and I actually had to work together to get information and move things along. At times, the seller was more helpful to me than my own solicitors.

Then Alison Buss took over and, incredibly, I had more communication from her in THREE DAYS than I had received from Ismail in SEVEN MONTHS.

This was the largest purchase of my life, yet I felt completely unsupported, anxious and like a burden every time I contacted them. It felt like a second job having to constantly chase the people I was paying to handle it. I paid Apex Law to manage my purchase, not to make me manage them.

Completely unprofessional and unacceptable. I would never use Apex Law again.

After my experience, I looked at previous reviews and was particularly concerned to find another recent review describing almost identical issues with Ismail — being impossible to reach, not responding to emails or calls and causing delays. Apex Law responded that they could not trace the reviewer as a client because they had not made a formal complaint. I will now be making my own formal complaint, so hopefully this time the issue can actually be addressed.

one_star_reviews.text:
I wrote a much longer, detailed review for Paul at Prestige Vehicle Consultants but it was too long and was not accepted. That review can be found on the MX-5 Owner’s Club Forum.

In short, I bought a 2017 MX-5 RF Launch Edition from Paul that had one owner and a FULL SERVICE HISTORY. Paul repeatedly assured me that he would provide all receipts and log book only for the car to be delivered and have only four services in nine years. Paul disputed this and made it difficult for me to get a refund, repeatedly telling me ‘What did you expect on a low mileage car?’ only for me to respond ‘A full service history, as advertised.’ Finally, after a phone call and many, many emails threatening legal action, Paul finally relented and agreed to refund, but it was not easy. He also tried to make me return the car myself, to which I promptly told him there was no chance.

To summarise: I screwed up by trusting a slick-talking dealer with a nice garage in the countryside full of beautiful MX-5s, and wanting one so badly. I take my responsibility in trusting the reviews here and not being as scrupulous as normal in my inspection (see photos of the rotten underside -- although not uncommon on MX-5s). If future customers want to risk buying from Prestige Vehicle Consultants, then I suggest to be extremely wary, diligent, and get everything in writing, along with getting the car inspected by an independent mechanic. Alas, aside from the weeks of stress and approximately £120 in fuel and insurance/tax that I never got back, I got my refund for the car and now the hunt continues. Best of luck to everyone else with this questionable garage. I, for one, will never go near it again.

I’m not a person who visits the doctor often so I’m unfamiliar with these things. After this experience I won’t be going back unless it’s life and death! I do have to add though that the reception staff were amazing. one_star_reviews.text: Awful! Do not send a loved ones here they deteriorate, inhumane way of treating people. My mother also left the facility with bed sores. I have evidence of this. If you wish to know more I have detailed information.

My wife entered Uplands with the hope of regaining strength, independence and confidence after suffering a stroke, through rehabilitation. Instead, since she was admitted to there care, we witnessed a significant decline in her physical condition. Rather than becoming stronger, she became noticeably weaker and is now largely bed bound. Prior to her admission in July she had successfully managed four months at home with appropriate support and equipment, maintaining a far greater level of independence than she has after her stay at Uplands.  As a family, we are deeply saddened by the deterioration we witnessed, as it is the very opposite of what we expected from a rehabilitation facility.
The most shocking issue was that my wife was instructed by members of staff to use her incontinence pad to pass a bowel movement rather than being assisted to the toilet or commode. I found this completely unacceptable and degrading. Even more concerning, she has told me that she was then left sitting in soiled pads for hours before being attended to.
I have also been informed she was regularly washed in bed because the shower in her room was out of order. We paid a considerable
amount of money for her room and the facilities
that come with it, yet she was unable to use the shower because it had not been repaired. Whilst bed washing may occasionally be clinically necessary, it should not become the default because basic facilities are unavailable. This is not an acceptable standard for a self-funding resident.
We are also appalled that my wife has returned home with multiple pressure sores (bed sores). The district nurse examined these and we have been informed that they appear to have been present for several days. This raises serious concerns about the care she received.
It is in my opinion you should avoid placing any loved ones in this facility!

one_star_reviews.text:
Very disappointing experience

I’ve found it incredibly difficult to get appointments at this surgery. The system relies heavily on telephone appointments, but you can be called at virtually any time of day, making it very easy to miss the call if you have work, children or a busy schedule. If you miss it, you then have to start the process again, which is extremely frustrating. Face-to-face appointments also seem very difficult to get.

Some of the reception staff are lovely, but unfortunately I’ve also experienced one member of staff who is extremely rude and unhelpful. I often feel like you don’t get much support from reception.

I’ve also found some of the doctors to be quite dismissive. On one occasion, I was simply advised to take Calpol, which I found incredibly unhelpful and felt like my concerns weren’t being properly listened to.

Ironically, the best clinician I’ve seen at the surgery is actually the paramedic. He listens, takes concerns seriously and makes you feel properly heard. Unfortunately, you never know which clinician you’re going to get, so it can feel like a lottery.

The whole experience has become so stressful and frustrating that we have now had no choice but to move to a different GP surgery. It’s really disappointing that it has come to this, but I feel the appointment system and consistency of care need a serious rethink

one_star_reviews.text:
They asked me to leave, and honestly, I feel it may have been because of racism85%

I got to the lake and had barely started setting up my gear when he started pointing out one issue after another. I explained that I hadn’t changed my hooks and rigs because I had been fishing at a wild, unmanaged lake beforehand. I’ll attach a video so you can see that the place was basically overgrown and full of weed.

I did have braided line, which was one issue, and there were also two hooks that weren’t barbless he said. However, the barbs had already been broken off, so they weren’t actually visible and they weren’t causing any damage to the fish.

Anyway, I understand the rules, and I’m not arguing with that. What I don’t understand is why I was told to leave and treated like some stray dog.

I could have easily changed the rigs. I had my tackle and tools with me, and I knew they had a shop there where I could have bought the correct hooks if necessary. I would have been more than happy to sort everything out and follow their rules.

I’ve also noticed that someone else seems to have had a similar experience, and I don’t think it’s right to treat a beginner like that or tell them “haven’t got time for this” simply because you don’t believe them or you don’t have pacience with the beginners customer!

And just to make it clear, I’m not Muslim, if that’s relevant to anyone. It’s not fair to blame all of us who work hard for the actions of people who steal or cause trouble.

Thanks for the hospitality! 👍

one_star_reviews.text: I am posting this regarding the awful service and treatment my son had when renting Flat 1 Clarendon Mews through M Coleman.  This was my son’s first experience of moving away from the family home and I found the flat for him on rightmove.  The flat was damp from the outset and this problem was ignored.  The flat was not in a good state of repair either one kitchen drawer front falling on my foot causing bruising when visiting within a few weeks of him moving in.  Then the rat infestation started.  M Coleman did nothing and were in fact very dismissive and rude.  I paid the office a visit and the lies they told were off the scale saying my son never reported the issues.  He has a file of evidence to support that he in fact did report repeatedly.  My husband paid a visit to the property to unblock drains to try to sort the damp issue as no-one else would do this.  Unfortunately my son was unable to stay in the flat due to the rat infestation, even the light fittings moved where the rats were running in the ceiling.  M Coleman found my son another property when he reported health issues due to the damp in the flat.  He moved out the weekend (sorry to those who are moving in).  The landlord would not let them go early but not only that, after myself and my daughter cleaned the property to the standard it was moved into in September including having the oven cleaned (and the bloody drawer front falling on my foot again), my son received a letter to say some of the bottom of the doors were “dusty” and a few other downright lies and suggest that the landlord will withhold the deposit.  I have photo evidence of the damp and mould and the condition the property was left in.  This company are a disgrace, cruel vile bullies.  My son has been so unwell physically and mentally dealing with this property, the nasty landlord and M Coleman’s gaslighting tactics that I have had to step in to support him.  This review outlines only a fraction of what he has had to deal with.  I have never known anything like this in my life.  These are my photos, there’s a huge file held by my son that documents MUCH more.  Please - stay away from this inhumane bunch of liars and crooks.
